names.form: Filumen de la Fântâna lui Iacov
names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 29 noiembrie, «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Filumen de la Fântâna lui Iacov», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 16 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιος Φιλούμενος ο Νεοιερομάρτυρας», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the title on the name link behind his line for 16 ноября ст. ст., name page 14538, «Филумен (Хасапис) Святогробец, архимандрит, сщмч.», with the grade and rank words left off. The surname in brackets and the epithet of the Holy Sepulchre are both part of the name the calendar prints and both stay; the day’s own line declines the name and keeps the epithet but not the surname. No other folder holds this form or the bare «Филумен».

birth.note: doxologia.ro: «Sfântul Filumen (după numele de mirean Sofocle), s-a născut în Lefcosia la 15 Octombrie 1913.»

death.note: doxologia.ro: «la data de 8 Mai a anului 1979 a fost transferat la fântâna lui Iacov, unde a slujit până la moartea lui martirică, pe 29 Noiembrie a aceluiași an.»

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 16 ноября ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Филумена Святогробца (1979) (Иерус.).»

attestations.note: The line ends «(Иерус.)», the calendar’s own mark for a commemoration it keeps as the Church of Jerusalem’s rather than as a general Russian one. The day is recorded as the calendar prints it, 16 ноября ст. ст., and the mark is kept here because it is part of what the source says.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 29 noiembrie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Filumen de la Fântâna lui Iacov»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 16ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιος Φιλούμενος ο Νεοιερομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 16 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The head line gives him «(; - 1979)», and the folder already carries both a `birth` and a `death`, so **no `dates` are proposed**. The entry is plainly him: of the village of Orounta in the district of Morphou, twin son of Magdalene and George Oroundiotis, taught piety by his grandmother Loxandra, set alight by reading the life of John the Hut-burner, gone with his twin Elpidios to the monastery of Stavrovouni and after five years to the Holy Land, forty-six years in the service of the Patriarchate's brotherhood, and cut down at the hour of vespers at Jacob's Well. **The day needs the writer's eye.** The page itself writes «Στις 16 Νοεμβρίου 1979 μ.Χ. (29 Νοεμβρίου με το νέο ημερολόγιο)» — 16 November by the old calendar, 29 November by the new — and the corpus already keeps his Romanian feast on **29 November**, which is these thirteen days. So the Greek day page and the Romanian row are one commemoration reckoned two ways, not two commemorations; the row recorded here is the day page that was read, per BRIEF-GREEK §8, and whether the Greek row should instead read 29/11 to match is a question for the writer and not a reader's to settle. No `locations` and no hymn: the page prints none. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Pe Cel împreună fără de început Ieșit din insula Cipru, ai venit la Sion, mucenicind la fântâna lui Iacov și primind tăierea capului și a degetelor. Iar cortul tău Hristos făcându-l nestricăcios, l-a arătat fântână de bogate daruri și felurite tămăduiri, sfinte sfințite mucenice Filumen.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul noului sfințit mucenic Filumen

english.text: Gone out from the island of Cyprus, you came to Sion, bearing witness at Jacob's well and receiving the cutting of your head and of your fingers. And Christ, making your tabernacle incorrupt, showed it a well of rich gifts and of healings of every kind, holy hieromartyr Philoumenos.
